sections.heading: Open-meteo Weather API

sections.heading: Rest Countries
paragraphs: Start with the basics. REST Countries is a free public API with structured data on every country — no key required.

The upshot: Countries, capitals, currencies, languages, time zones and borders come back as clean JSON, and the service is explicitly free for any use. It is the kind of dataset that makes a side project feel twice as finished.

sections.heading: Wikipedia API
paragraphs: The foundation looks like this: Wikipedia's API is free, keyless and practically unbounded for personal projects.

The upshot: Search, summaries, and full article text in JSON or wikitext are all available over plain HTTP. The only rule that matters is politeness: identify your app in the User-Agent and do not hammer the service.
For a personal project or side business, this covers you without breaking a sweat.
